record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; result files and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports behavioral results from weight-edited, ablated model pairs, testing practical removal of refusal rather than the original residual-stream projection and addition method.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal-rate changes on harmful-request sets and paired results for tool calling and injection attacks. The listed JSON result files were not read. It reports no test of adding the direction, and no model-size trend result because H3 is described as not testable. H1/H2/H4-style outcomes are recorded as findings outside the listed claim versions where the README does not test the version's named intervention or measure.
record.test_reason: It measures refusal rates on harmful-request sets for released abliterated or Heretic weights against their stock checkpoints. That bears directly on V2, in a new setting: third-party uploads, Q8_0 quantisation, llama.cpp serving and a shared chat template. It does not extract or add a difference-in-means direction, so V1 and the other versions are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct but incomplete. The authors also state that the predicted direction, tool-call degradation and higher injection susceptibility, 'appears nowhere'. The cross-family Llama pair passed the refusal check but its tool-call and injection suites could not be scored. The authors stress that nothing generalises beyond one family.
record.recipe_differences: This is a research harness/tool repo, not a replication of the original method. It compares stock models with released abliterated weights and evaluates refusal, tool calling, injection, and other controls; it does not identify the difference-in-means direction or perform the original all-layer projection and addition interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary across model pairs and prompt sets. The README notes that 0.6B did not pass the refusal-removal gate, that 4B and 8B manipulation checks were repeated on other corpora, and that the cross-family Llama tool-call and injection suites could not be fully scored because of serving errors.

fits_no_version.finding: Tool-call accuracy after abliteration shows no consistent degradation. Three pairs are equivalent and the 14B pair improves by 5.3 pp. The 14B gain is largely because the ablated arm no longer emits refusals that the strict grader counts as wrong tool calls.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Released abliterated Qwen3 models keep structured tool-call accuracy within a pre-registered SESOI or improve on it.

fits_no_version.finding: Indirect prompt-injection attack success does not consistently rise after abliteration. The 4B ablated arm is less susceptible (-6.3 pp), two pairs are equivalent, and 14B is inconclusive (+3.7 pp).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing the refusal direction does not consistently increase compliance with injected tool-result instructions.

fits_no_version.finding: The Llama pair's general-capability score is unchanged (86%→86%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliteration leaves a general-capability control score intact in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.

record.problems: This is a repo README rather than a peer-reviewed study text, and the result JSON files were not read. The README reports five Qwen3 pairs, with one ablation-unverified pair and a single cross-family Llama pair whose tool-call and injection suites were cut short by serving errors. All five primary pairs are from one model family; the README also notes shared-template intervention for some published ablated arms, quantisation, one temperature and seed, and hardware/serving constraints.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted from the listed result JSON files because their contents were not part of the read text. The README's qualitative H4 labels for Qwen3 pairs are not assigned numerical outcome rows because it provides no corresponding values there. The Llama tool-call and injection data are not scored as outcomes because the README says the suites were incomplete and could not be scored on that serving stack.

untested.parts: Model families other than Qwen3 beyond a single Llama-3.1-8B pair. The 0.6B, 1.7B and 14B pairs ran only on the authored-100 set. No unquantised or full-precision serving. One temperature and one seed. Ablated arms were served with a shared template, not exactly as published.

missing.what: Benign over-refusal 0%→0% on the Llama pair. The Llama first-token KL is 1.03 [0.85, 1.23] with top-1 agreement 0.45, far above the Qwen3 pairs (0.009–0.235).
Clean-control tool-use divergence (S1): 14B +7.1 pp, 8B +4.5 pp, 4B -5.3 pp. Also lenient grading (S4), under which the 4B H1 effect disappears (89.8% in both arms).
Per-cell stock and ablated refusal rates, b/c counts and CIs for the corpus replications and the authored-100 runs.

record.verdict_notes: This is a pre-registered GitHub README, not peer-reviewed, and the result JSON files were not read. The study's main question is about side effects of abliteration (H1, H2), which fall outside the listed versions. Its manipulation check is what bears on V2. The 0.6B 'ablation-unverified' status reflects a gate artefact: refusal still reached 0%.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is identified and projected out at every residual-stream layer and position; no direction-addition test; reported weight edits do not test the original intervention.

The study does not establish results for abliteration generally; most pairs are Qwen3, and the README reports one scorable cross-family refusal result. It does not report refusal outcomes on every possible harmful-request set or released model.
No attack is reported as suppressing the refusal direction, and no training against the direction's ablation is tested.
No affine, cone, or multiple-direction representation is tested.
No separation between harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is tested.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.

relation.reason: Its own stock-vs-ablated refusal results bear directly on whether released abliterated models stop refusing (V2).

tranche.reason: Measures refusal rates of third-party released abliterated/Heretic weights against stock arms (paired McNemar) in a new setting: Q8_0, llama.cpp ROCm, shared template. This is a result on V2, though refusal is only the study's manipulation check; its main question is tool calling and injection, so not T2.

source_check.notes: Ablated-arm refusal is stated only for 0.6B (0%) and Llama (0%); 4B AdvBench's 99 pp drop implies at most 1% left. All Qwen arms ran on one shared Qwen template (sha a55ee1b1), Q8_0, llama.cpp ROCm, temp 0.0, seed 1234.
